description:
Search a structure database with a small number of reference structures

The structure-input counterpart of domain_search.py. For searching large structure
databases (for example a foldseek database built from AlphaFold DB) with a handful of
reference structures.

Only records that had a hit are written. Each one carries a Domain_Search feature marking
the region homologous to the best-matching reference; pass --add_annotations to also write
a Domainator feature for every hit.

References are aligned as the query and the searched database as the target, which is both
what foldseek is optimized for and what makes --evalue mean the same thing it means
elsewhere in domainator: it is computed against the database being searched. The hit
coordinates are positions on the database record; the matching positions on the reference
are recorded in the /rstart, /rend and /rlen qualifiers.

Hit records are built from the sequences the backend reports, so the searched database is
never read end to end and its size does not bound memory. Note that --max_seqs bounds how
many hits the backend keeps per reference; the default is low for a large database, and a
warning is issued whenever a reference saturates it.

Use structure_domainate.py instead to annotate every input structure rather than select
hits, and structure_to_genbank.py to convert structures without searching at all.

parameters.name: Input
parameters.help: the structure database to search: the prefix of a prebuilt foldseek database, or pdb/cif files (optionally gzipped), a directory to search recursively, or a glob.

parameters.name: References
parameters.help: reference structures to search with. Same accepted forms as --input.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.help: output genbank filename. If not supplied, or if given as '-', writes to stdout.

parameters.name: Evalue
parameters.help: threshold E value for a hit. E values are computed against the searched database.

parameters.name: Max Hits
parameters.help: return at most this many records, the best-scoring ones. Applies to the whole search, not per reference. When set, output is sorted best-first and written after the search completes.

parameters.name: Max Seqs
parameters.help: maximum number of hits to keep per reference, keeping the most significant ones. Defaults to the backend's own default: 1000 for foldseek, no cap for reseek. For foldseek this bounds the search itself, so raising it costs time but improves coverage; for reseek it bounds only the output, since reseek has no native cap and does the full search either way. A warning is printed whenever a reference saturates the cap.

parameters.name: Alignment Type
parameters.help: foldseek only: how to compute the alignment: 0 = 3Di only, 1 = TM-align, 2 = 3Di+AA (the default when unset). Type 1 requires C-alpha coordinates in both databases. reseek has no alignment-type option and rejects this.

parameters.name: Metrics
parameters.help: additional per-hit structural metrics to compute and store as feature qualifiers. tmscore, lddt and rmsd require C-alpha coordinates in both databases.

parameters.name: Cpu
parameters.help: number of threads to give the backend. 0 lets the backend use all available cores.

parameters.name: Device
parameters.help: where to run the search. 'cpu' for a CPU-only search, or a CUDA device string ('cuda', 'cuda:0', 'cuda:1', ...) for a GPU-accelerated search. GPU search requires a recent foldseek. [default: cpu]

parameters.name: Add Annotations
parameters.help: also write a Domainator feature for every hit, in addition to the Domain_Search feature for the best hit.

advanced_parameters.name: Min Evalue
advanced_parameters.help: minimum E value for a hit. Useful for excluding a reference's match to its own copy in the database.

advanced_parameters.name: Max Overlap
advanced_parameters.help: maximum fraction of overlap allowed between annotations on one record. 1 disables overlap filtering.

advanced_parameters.name: Overlap By Db
advanced_parameters.help: filter overlapping annotations within each database independently, instead of across all databases.

advanced_parameters.name: Database Name
advanced_parameters.help: value for the /database qualifier on the annotations. Defaults to the reference database or directory name.

advanced_parameters.name: Keep Db
advanced_parameters.help: when the input is structure files rather than a prebuilt database, also write the database built from them, using this path as its prefix.

advanced_parameters.name: Hits Tsv
advanced_parameters.help: write the aligner's own hit table here, for debugging or for cross-checking against a hand-run search. With reseek this is the table before the per-reference cap is applied, so it may hold more rows than the output.

advanced_parameters.name: Foldseek Path
advanced_parameters.help: path to the foldseek executable. If not supplied, foldseek is looked up on PATH.

advanced_parameters.name: Aligner Arg
advanced_parameters.help: extra arguments appended verbatim to the backend's search command line, for options domainator does not wrap. Example: --aligner_arg --prefilter-mode 2

advanced_parameters.name: Tmp Dir
advanced_parameters.help: parent directory for temporary databases and alignment files. Structural searches can need a lot of scratch space, so point this at a large filesystem for big inputs.

advanced_parameters.name: Max Output Gb
advanced_parameters.help: Fail if a projected output file would exceed this many GB. Set to 0 to disable the guardrail.

advanced_parameters.name: Reseek Path
advanced_parameters.help: path to the reseek executable. If not supplied, reseek is looked up on PATH.

advanced_parameters.name: Reseek Stats
advanced_parameters.help: reseek only: SCOP level that reseek's p-value model is calibrated against. This shifts p-values by orders of magnitude, so it changes which hits pass the E-value threshold. Ignored by other backends.

advanced_parameters.name: Reseek Sensitivity
advanced_parameters.help: reseek only: search sensitivity. Ignored by other backends.
